operating_notes.text: Crisil rates ₹34 Cr of Cheviot's bank facilities: ₹10 Cr cash credit and ₹22 Cr non-fund based limit from Axis Bank, plus a ₹2 Cr proposed term loan.
Q4FY26 other income was -₹23.67 Cr, primarily loss on fair valuation of FVTPL investments, versus -₹5.53 Cr in Q4FY25.
FY26 other comprehensive income includes ₹1,031.79 lakh (net of tax) revaluation surplus on freehold land in the prior year; FY26 OCI was ₹6.13 Cr net of tax.
The company recognised ₹18.91 lakh incremental past service cost on post-employment benefits after the New Labour Codes took effect on 21 November 2025.

Office of the Jute Commissioner notified revisions to maximum ex-factory prices for 580 gms B-Twill Sacking Jute bags for Jan 2021 to Dec 2023 supplies, expected to increase Cheviot's sales realisation by ~₹19 Cr.

timeline.summary: On 21 April 2026, Crisil reaffirmed Cheviot's long-term rating at Crisil A+/Stable and short-term at Crisil A1+ on ₹34 Cr of rated bank facilities, valid till 31 March 2027.
Utkarsh Kanoria, Harsh Vardhan Kanoria, Malati Kanoria, and promoter group entities declared no encumbrance on Cheviot Company shares for FY2025-26.
Office of the Jute Commissioner revised ex-factory prices for Jan 2021–Dec 2023 supplies, boosting Cheviot's sales realisation by ~₹19 Cr.
